html:
The Anaiwan, also written Anēwan or Nganyaywana, are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Tablelands of New South Wales, in high country around present day Armidale.

Their neighbours were the Gamilaraay to the west, the Gumbaynggirr and Dunghutti toward the coast and the Ngarabal to the north. Squatters took up the New England tablelands in the 1830s and 1840s. The Anaiwan language was poorly recorded, and since 2017 a project has worked to bring it back. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Anaiwan, also written Anēwan or Nganyaywana, are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Tablelands of New South Wales, in high country around present day Armidale.
